The Department of Innovation & Technology (DoIT) is seeking to hire qualified candidates with the opportunity to work in a dynamic, creative thinking, problem solving environment. This position serves as a Systems Command Center Technician on the day shift for the Department of Innovation & Technology (DoIT) performing journey level enterprise system and network operations control work. In this role you will monitor, operate, and control systems and peripheral devices and environments to ensure appropriate availability and status resources. In addition, you will monitor various systems and contact on-call staff to resolve any unresolved issues, such as system and server failures. If you possess these knowledges, skills, abilities, and experience, we invite you to apply for this position to join the DoIT Team! As a State of Illinois employee, you receive a comprehensive benefits package including: Competitive Group Insurance benefits including health, life, dental and vision plans. Flexible work schedules (when available and dependent upon position). 10 -25 days of paid vacation time annually (10 days for first year of state employment). 12 days of paid sick time annually which carry over year to year. 3 paid personal business days per year. 13-14 paid holidays per year dependent on election years. 12 weeks of paid parental leave. Pension plan through the State Employees Retirement System. Deferred Compensation Program – voluntary supplemental retirement plan. Optional pre-tax programs -Medical Care Assistance Plan (MCAP) & Dependent Care Assistant Plan (DCAP). Tuition Reimbursement Program and Federal Public Service Loan Forgiveness Program eligibility. For more information regarding State of Illinois Benefits follow this link: https://www2.illinois.gov/cms/benefits/Pages/default.aspx Essential Functions Under general supervision, serves as a System Command Center Technician for the Department of Innovation & Technology (DoIT), performing journey-level enterprise system and network operations control work and computer control functions, including performing startups, shutdowns, system dumps (tasks, system, spool, etc.) and other functions for controlling a multi-processing computer environment. Monitors mainframe systems and logs and responds to system issues to ensure appropriate availability of resources, including researching, resolving, and circumventing interruptions to processing components by following standard operational processes, procedures, and checklists. Keeps abreast of new developments in the information technology field by continuing education through online training platforms, attending meetings, training sessions, seminars, and conferences to increase familiarity with and remain current on products, vendors, techniques, and procedures. Performs other duties as required or assigned which are reasonably within the scope of the duties enumerated above. Minimum Qualifications Requires knowledge, skill, and mental development equivalent to completion of high school. Requires one (1) year of related data processing experience. Qualifying state employees in the employee Upward Mobility Program (UMP), may complete combinations of specific proficiency tests and training programs leading to a certificate of proficiency in lieu of the stated requirements for this classification. Preferred Qualifications (In Order Of Significance) One (1) year of professional experience monitoring enterprise mainframe computer systems in a large-scale, multi-platform environment, including overseeing system performance, availability, and resource utilization by operating, monitoring, or controlling enterprise computer systems through automated tools, z/OS system commands, and menu-driven mainframe operations. Working knowledge of mainframe operational system commands, including stops and restarts, system IPLs, and online commands using automated processes, in accordance with established procedures and checklists. Ability to clearly document incidents, actions, and resolutions, to compile and maintain accurate shift logs and to update tickets to support audit and compliance requirements. Ability to monitor, analyze, and resolve system errors and interruptions, by applying standard operating procedures, written check-list procedures, and contacting on-call techs. Ability to analyze data logically and exercise sound judgement in defining and evaluating problems of an operational or procedural nature. Ability to gain and maintain effective working relationships with associates, vendors, clients, and others. Developed verbal and written communication skills to present technical information clearly and precisely to diverse audiences, including business users, development teams, and agency executives. Requires the ability to work outside of normal hours to meet deadlines. Requires the ability to use agency supplied equipment such as laptop, personal computer, work cell phone, etc. Requires the ability to work overtime including scheduled, unscheduled, short notice, evening, weekends, and holidays. Requires the ability to attend seminars, conferences, and training to remain current on methods, tools, ideologies, or other industry related topics relevant to job duties. The SharePoint Administrator provides technical support in administering, updating, and maintaining the CIO and DCS G-6 SharePoint environment in support of Army business systems. This position also supports Microsoft 365, data visualization, knowledge management, and records and information management activities to help the organization manage, organize, locate, track, report, and present information maintained within SharePoint and other authorized information repositories. The Administrator works directly with Government leadership, Site Owners, information owners, and end users to define requirements, implement changes, maintain governance standards, and ensure content accuracy and system performance. This role reports to the Site Lead and Program Manager. This is an onsite position at Ft. Belvoir, VA. About ITility ITility is a Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Business with a passion to equip our nation’s Intelligence Community, armed forces and first responders with the very best to empower their missions. From the virtual battlefield to boots on the ground, our people, processes, and performance drive our ability to help our clients protect what matters, now and for generations to come. At ITility , we help our customers command the future by thinking beyond perceived limits to create new, unexpected ways to protect and defend our nation. We inspire and empower people to create significant solutions that secure what matters to our customers and communities, here and around the globe. We Value: The Drive to Perform Beyond Perceived Limits. The Desire to Find Significance in All We Do. The Passion and Compassion That Powers Both. Key Responsibilities: SharePoint Administration and Governance Serve as the primary administrator for the CIO and DCS G-6 SharePoint environment. Administer, maintain, and enhance SharePoint sites, libraries, lists, permissions, metadata, workflows, and content-management structures. Maintain, update, and ensure accuracy of homepage, documents, and site content. Enforce governance standards for site creation, permissions management, and content lifecycle. Maintain HUB site permissions and role-based access controls. Ensure CAC authentication and compliance with Army business system security requirements. Adhere to Standard Development Life Cycle (SDLC) processes and applicable web policies. Technical Support and Ticket Resolution Provide Tier I maintenance and technical support for approved applications. Respond to and resolve SharePoint-related help desk tickets daily. Track, document, and formally manage site change requests. Provide troubleshooting support for user access, site functionality, and content updates. Generate and submit monthly ticketing reports. Content Management and Modernization Work directly with customers to define SharePoint requirements and translate them into site design, structure, and functionality. Develop collaborative SharePoint sites, lists, libraries, and workflows. Develop SharePoint-based tracking solutions and automated workflows supporting records, correspondence, information requests, suspenses, and organizational business processes. Develop and maintain Power BI dashboards, reports, metrics, and data visualizations using authorized organizational data to support leadership visibility, workload tracking, records management, and other mission requirements. Leverage Power Automate and other Government-approved Microsoft 365 capabilities to support workflow automation and information visibility. Support records and information management activities consistent with applicable Army, DoD, and NARA records-management requirements. Assist with organizing, indexing, categorizing, searching, retrieving, and compiling electronic records from SharePoint and other authorized repositories. Support records searches associated with FOIA requests, including locating and organizing potentially responsive records, maintaining request and status tracking information, documenting search activities, and preparing records for review by authorized Government personnel. Support document libraries, metadata structures, retention organization, archival processes, records inventories, and disposition-related activities. Ensure all new web applications conform to approved design and formatting standards. Test and monitor SharePoint performance regularly. Conduct regular link verification and coordinate content archival. Identify and account for Site Owners and provide guidance and training resources. Support migration efforts to Microsoft 365 and SharePoint Online platforms. Leverage migration tools and automation where appropriate. Government personnel retain responsibility and authority for official FOIA determinations, exemption decisions, redactions, and release of Government information. Reporting and Deliverables Maintain homepage and organizational content as required. Provide monthly homepage usage statistics reports. Provide monthly ticketing reports using approved systems (Remedy, KACE, AESD, or successor platforms). Maintain records-management and information-request tracking dashboards showing approved status, suspense, workload, aging, search status, and related metrics. Develop technical documentation, SOPs, user guides, and training materials related to SharePoint, information management, dashboards, and associated workflows. Participate in weekly or bi-weekly SharePoint synchronization meetings. Provide leadership updates as required. Support backup procedures and restoration of SharePoint environments as needed. Scope of Support The SharePoint environment supports hundreds of authenticated Army users across multiple CIO and DCS G-6 entities, including collaborative workspaces, organizational portals, and cross-functional mission systems on classified and unclassified networks. The Administrator must be capable of supporting multiple organizations simultaneously while maintaining governance, security compliance, and performance standards. Required Qualifications: Active Secret Clearance. Bachelor’s Degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, or related field, or a minimum of four years of relevant IT web technology experience. Demonstrated experience administering SharePoint 2013, 2016, and/or SharePoint Online. Experience supporting Microsoft 365 environments. Strong understanding of SharePoint architecture, permissions models, governance frameworks, and SDLC processes. Experience translating customer requirements into functional web solutions. Ability to communicate effectively with business leadership, technical leadership, and engineers. Experience supporting DoD or Federal environments preferred. Professional Attributes: Detail-oriented and process-driven. Mission-focused and customer-responsive. Strong communicator with professional presence. Capable of balancing technical execution with governance oversight. Desired Skills: Experience developing Power BI dashboards and reports. Experience with Power Automate workflow development. Experience migrating from on-premises or non-Microsoft platforms to Microsoft 365. Experience with Artificial Intelligence. Familiarity with migration tools and automation. Familiarity with electronic records and information management. Familiarity with NARA federal records-management principles. Familiarity with FOIA records-search and request-tracking processes. Ability to conduct structured electronic records searches and document search methodology. Knowledge of Army web policy and CAC-enabled environments. Strong understanding of access controls and handling sensitive Government information. Strong documentation and reporting skills. Ability to operate independently in a dynamic operational environment. Physical Requirements: Work is typically performed in an office setting. Prolonged periods of sitting at a desk and working on a computer. Must have the ability to lift 15-25 pounds.
